title: opportunity-windowing for prefill/decode with QoS buckets and fair credits
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Problem: Current prefill/decode arbitration prioritizes either low-latency single-shot decodes or high-throughput long-running jobs but struggles in mixed workloads. This leads to either increased P95 latency for small interactive requests during bursts or suboptimal GPU utilization when many short decodes are scheduled aggressively. We need a scheduler that preserves tail latency for interactive traffic while opportunistically improving throughput and kernel utilization where possible.

Proposal summary: Implement an "opportunity-windowing" scheduling policy that: (1) assigns each incoming request to a short sliding opportunity window based on predicted remaining token length and QoS bucket, (2) groups windows across similar phase positions and attention/kernel-cost profiles to enable batched decodes and kernel-friendly prefill coalescing, and (3) uses a per-tenant credit-based fairness mechanism to bound long-running jobs so they don't starve interactive traffic. The policy works at the prefill/decode phase boundary and integrates with kernel selection heuristics and attention-optimization hints to choose decode fastpaths when latency-sensitive and throughput-optimized kernels for opportunistic batches.
motivation_and_goals: Preserve P95/P99 latency for latency-sensitive (tiered) traffic during mixed workloads.
Improve tokens/s GPU utilization by consolidating compatible decode windows without creating excessive queuing for interactive requests.
Give predictable performance for Dedicated customers via QoS buckets and enforceable credit budgets.
Expose operational metrics (window hit rate, credit drains, kernel-selection mismatches) to Console for troubleshooting and tuning.
design_decisions: Opportunity windows are short (configurable default 10-50ms) and slide based on arrival time + predicted decoding horizon rather than fixed phases, reducing fragmentation under bursty input.
QoS buckets: 'latency', 'balanced', 'throughput' mapped to per-tenant credit refill rates and max window wait times. Latency bucket bypasses opportunistic batching unless wait < 5ms.
Credit model: long-running jobs accrue negative credits proportional to outstanding tokens; periodic refill prevents permanent starvation but enforces bounded resource share.

Kernel hints: requests carry attention-profile fingerprints (sequence length distribution, relative KV-cache reuse) computed during prefill. Scheduler chooses kernel family (low-latency fastpath vs fused-kernel throughput) based on aggregated window profile.
KV cache coalescing: when prefill windows align for the same model/version and contiguous token prefixes, we reuse a shared KV-subgraph to reduce memory pressure and speedups for decode batches.
Compatibility fallback: when kernel mismatch or memory constraints prevent coalescing, requests are hedged with single-request fastpath to avoid tail regressions.
acceptance_criteria: P95 latency for latency-bucket requests increases by <5% compared to baseline under mixed workload (30% interactive, 70% long-running).
Aggregate GPU tokens/s increases by >=10% on mixed synthetic workload (80k token-minutes baseline).
No more than 0.5% of latency-bucket requests see queuing > 50ms in production canary at 5% traffic.
Operational metrics surfaced in Console: window_hit_rate, credit_balance_histogram, kernel_selection_mismatch_rate, and per-tenant fairness_score.
Automated integration tests for window boundary conditions, credit exhaustion/replenishment, and kernel mismatch hedging.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design + simulation): implement opportunity-windowing simulator in Go to evaluate parameter sensitivity and fairness under varied mixes (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (runtime prototype): add scheduling layer in serving runtime that tags requests with window_id and credit tokens; integrate kernel hint propagation in prefill path (3 weeks).

Phase 3 (benchmarks): run on staging cluster with representative models (small/med/long) and synthetic clients to measure latency/throughput trade-offs; tune default window sizes and credit refill curves (2 weeks).
Phase 4 (canary rollout): feature-flagged canary starting at 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with rollback conditions; collect Console metrics and user-impact alerts (2 weeks).
Phase 5 (hardening): add observability, rate-limit guards, and configuration knobs per-deployment (Dedicated/Private) and release docs (1 week).
engineering_tasks: ENG: subsystem: scheduler - add Window Manager and per-tenant credit ledger (runtime/scheduler.go, ~600 LOC).
ENG: prefill: compute lightweight attention fingerprints and predicted remaining tokens; expose in request metadata.
ENG: kernel-selection: accept aggregated window profile and select kernel family; add mismatch detection path for hedging.
ENG: KV-cache: implement opportunistic KV-subgraph sharing with eviction safety checks.
ENG: telemetry: emit window_id, window_wait_ms, credit_balance, kernel_family, and coalesce_hit boolean to observability pipeline.
ENG: tests: unit tests for credit accounting, integration tests for end-to-end latency under synthetic mixes, and load tests on staging.
experiments_and_results: Simulator run (mixed 30/70 interactive/long) with window=20ms, latency-refill fast: fairness_score=0.86 (higher is better), P95 latency delta +3%, tokens/s +12%.
Staging microbenchmark of 1 model ( 1.3B ) shows window coalescing reduced redundant KV copying by 18% and improved batch size distribution toward more 4-8 request batches during bursts.
Kernel mismatch observed at 4.7% of windows for long-tail attention shapes; hedging eliminated P99 spikes in follow-up run.
rollout_plan: Automated rollback on: P95 latency regression > 8% for latency bucket OR increased error rate > 0.2% OR credit_balances indicate starvation events > 0.5% of tenants.
Post-deploy: 1 week of daily checks and a retrospective runbook documenting tuning knobs.
observability_and_alerting: New Console charts: per-tenant window_hit_rate, kernel_selection_mismatch_rate, credit_balance_percentile.
Alerts: high_starvation (credit_balance < 0 for >1% tenants over 5m), kernel_mismatch_burst (>2% windows in 1m), degraded_latency_bucket_p95.
Tracing: add span tags for window_id and kernel_family to decode traces for root-cause of regressions.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggregation could increase tail latency for unusual attention shapes. Mitigation: hedging and kernel mismatch detection to fall back to fastpath.
Risk: Credit algorithm tuning complexity may frustrate Dedicated customers. Mitigation: expose per-tenant knobs and default conservative refill rates; provide Dashboard to inspect credit use.
Risk: KV-cache sharing may increase memory pressure with many unique prefixes. Mitigation: conservative sharing thresholds + LRU subgraph eviction policy.
